zones.what: Deck 1 cabins 1409, 1410, 1414, 1415 and Deck 2 cabins 2109, 2110 have small round portholes rather than windows, and the view out is partly blocked by lifeboats or other ship equipment.
zones.effect: Guests get natural light through the porthole but a narrower, sometimes blocked, look at the horizon rather than a clear picture-window view.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone booking a porthole cabin expecting a clean sea view; doesn't matter to guests who just want cheap outside light.
zones.source: cruisebooking.com and shinecruise.com both independently name the same Deck 1/2 cabin numbers with lifeboat/equipment obstruction
zones.confidenceNote: corroborated across two independent ship-specific listicles

zones.what: All forward Deck 3 cabins (roughly 3101–3143) are Interior-type staterooms whose window looks out onto an outside walkway/observation area rather than directly to sea, with lifeboats and lifeboat equipment visible beyond, and the glass is tinted so passers-by on the walkway can't see in.
zones.effect: You get a window and daylight, but the 'view' is really an access walkway shared with other guests, with lifeboat gear in the background — a look-alike ocean-view cabin that isn't a clean sea view.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests booking these on the assumption of an unobstructed sea view; doesn't matter much to budget-focused cruisers who just want a window cabin.
zones.source: cruisemapper.com deck-3 page: "Lobby Deck passenger cabins from 3101 to 3143 ... Interior with walkway view / obstructed"; corroborated by shinecruise.com's parallel Sunrise page describing the same category as obstructed by lifeboats and lifeboat equipment

zones.what: Deck 8 aft cabins sit directly beneath the Lido pool/buffet/Havana Bar deck (Deck 9), and Deck 9 cabins sit under gym/spa deck 10 in forward sections.
zones.effect: Deck 8 aft cabins catch early-morning deck-chair dragging, deck parties and buffet foot traffic from directly overhead; Deck 9 forward cabins (around 9138–9139 and forward) sit under the fitness area and can pick up workout noise.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and anyone wanting a lie-in should avoid these; doesn't matter to guests who are up early and out of the cabin anyway.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com Deck 8 page: "more likely an issue for the cabins on the aft of the deck which are below the buffet and Havana Bar areas"; Deck 9 page: "Cabins between 9138 and 9139 and forward are below the gym area on the deck above and could experience noise issues"

zones.what: The lowest aft guest cabins sit closest to the engine room and machinery spaces.
zones.effect: Some low-deck aft cabins pick up engine hum/vibration that higher, more midship cabins don't.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to noise- and vibration-sensitive guests; less relevant to those who sleep through anything and want the cheapest fare.
zones.source: cruisebooking.com: "Lower deck cabins near an engine room (Deck 1 & 2 aft) will experience vibrations and noises from machinery"

zones.what: Deck 5 aft is home to Ocean Plaza, the casino, RedFrog Pub and the Limelight Lounge, all clustered together.
zones.effect: Cabins on this deck near the aft nightlife cluster hear music and crowd noise into the late evening.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers; nightlife-seekers may actually prefer the proximity.
zones.source: cruise.blog: "Deck 5 on Carnival Sunshine is another hub of activity, home to venues like Ocean Plaza, the Sunshine Casino, RedFrog Pub, and the Limelight Lounge"

zones.what: Some Deck 6 cabins sit directly above the casino or above the Limelight Theater on Deck 5.
zones.effect: First-person reports describe hearing show music and casino activity through the floor.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests wanting quiet; theatre-goers who go to bed late won't mind.
zones.source: cruise.blog citing guest reports: one stayed "above the casino and regretted it"; another "above the Limelight Theater" could hear show music

zones.what: Deck 8 cabins below and Deck 9 cabins near the RedFrog Rum Bar and BlueIguana Tequila Bar pick up bar noise.
zones.effect: Music and conversation from these poolside bars carry into nearby cabins on sea days and evenings.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone wanting an afternoon nap; bar-hoppers may like being close.
zones.source: shinecruise.com: "Cabins on Deck 8 that are below and Cabins on Deck 9 that are near the RedFrog Rum Bar and BlueIguana Tequila Bar can be noisy"

zones.what: Cabins directly beside or across from elevator/stair banks on Decks 6–9 sit next to constant door-chime and foot-traffic noise.
zones.effect: Convenient for quick access to public decks, but the trade-off is elevator-door noise and hallway traffic at all hours.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers and those sensitive to hallway noise; convenient for mobility-limited guests who want minimal walking.
zones.source: cruisebooking.com: rooms near elevators/staircases on "Decks 6, 7, 8, 9" hear "constant traffic noises, door slams, footsteps"

zones.what: The crew-only I-95 corridor runs on Deck 0, one level below the lowest guest cabin deck (Deck 1), connecting crew messes, laundry, and engine spaces bow to stern.
zones.effect: Passengers occasionally glimpse this corridor at the gangway or during tendering, and its stairwell/access points nearest Deck 1 can create brief service traffic near the lowest guest cabins.
zones.mattersTo: Barely matters to most guests; relevant only to Deck 1 bookers curious about occasional crew movement near stairwells.
zones.source: cruisehive.com: "I-95 will usually be on deck zero"; ProPublica CDC inspection log for Carnival Sunshine references a "Buffet-Deck 0 - Crew Mess", confirming Deck 0 as the crew corridor level on this ship

zones.what: Main propulsion machinery sits low and aft; the original Destiny-class design (unchanged in hull form for Sunshine) carries six transverse thrusters, three forward and three aft, in addition to the main engines.
zones.effect: Aft low-deck cabins are closest to engine vibration/hum, while both the bow and stern get thruster noise/vibration during docking and maneuvering — the aft thrusters are somewhat unusual and mean stern cabins aren't as thruster-quiet as on many other ships.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to vibration-sensitive sleepers, especially on port-heavy itineraries with frequent docking; less relevant to guests who spend little time in the cabin.
zones.source: cruisingjournal.com on the original Destiny-class hull: "equipped with six transverse thrusters (three forward and three aft)"; cruisebooking.com on Sunshine specifically: lower aft cabins near the engine room feel "vibrations and noises from machinery"

zones.what: The anchor chain and windlass sit low in the bow, and Carnival Sunshine's itineraries include tender ports (e.g., Half Moon Cay, Princess Cays) requiring anchoring.
zones.effect: Forward, lower-deck guests can hear the anchor chain running out and being hauled, typically in the early morning on tender-port days.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers on tender-port itineraries; irrelevant on pure-dock itineraries.
zones.source: cruise.blog: "Forward cabins on a lower deck may also hear the noisy anchor drop in tender ports like Half Moon Cay and Princess Cays"

zones.what: As on any ship, forward and aft cabins feel more pitch/roll than midship, and higher decks amplify roll versus lower decks.
zones.effect: One member review reported the ship "rocking left and right ALL THE TIME" even in fairly mild seas and needing medication despite prior cruise experience; a separate 2026 news report described Carnival Sunshine tilting hard enough to send objects sliding after a mechanical/technical issue.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to motion-sensitive guests choosing forward/aft or upper decks; less relevant to guests choosing midship, lower/mid decks.
zones.source: CruiseCritic member review of Carnival Sunshine: ship was "rocking left and right ALL THE TIME"; CBS News report: the ship "tipped to one side ... sending loose items sliding"

zones.what: Deck 6 interior cabins 6101–6106 and Deck 7 interior cabins 7101–7106 are described as having obstructed views because of lifeboats/tenders directly outside.
zones.effect: These specific interior cabin blocks lose what little forward outlook they might have to lifeboat/tender equipment.
zones.mattersTo: Matters only to guests booking these specific interior-with-window cabins expecting any kind of view.
zones.source: shinecruise.com: "Interior cabins with obstructed views include those on Deck 6 from cabins 6101 to 6106 and Deck 7 from cabins 7101 to 7106"

zones.what: Connecting staterooms ("family cabins") exist on Decks 1, 2, 6, 9, 10, and 11 across several categories (PT, 4E, 4G, 6A/B/C/D, 8S, 8T, 4J).
zones.effect: Connecting doors are convenient for families/groups but are thinner than a standard cabin wall, so sound (TV, conversation, kids) can pass through more easily than a normal partition.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to groups wanting linked rooms (a plus) and to solo/couple travelers randomly assigned next to a noisy connecting pair (a minus).
zones.source: cruisemapper.com: "Connecting staterooms ('family cabins') are located on Decks 1, 2, 6, 9, 10, and 11"; cruisecritic.com Editor's Review: Sunshine offers "more than 200 connecting rooms, which sometimes permits sound through the connecting doors"

zones.what: Premium Vista/wraparound balcony cabins (categories 8M/9C) are built to wrap around the aft corners of the ship on Decks 6 through 9, giving a larger balcony (up to ~75 sq ft) than the standard 35 sq ft balcony.
zones.effect: These corner cabins get a noticeably wider side-and-stern panorama than a standard side balcony, at the cost of being closer to whatever noise/activity sits at the aft end of that deck.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to view- and balcony-space-focused guests willing to pay for a premium/wraparound category; not a true hull-cantilever 'hump' extending past the hull line, just a corner-wrap design, so it doesn't change straight-down sightlines like a true hump would.
zones.source: carnival.com: "Premium Vista Balcony staterooms were designed to wrap around the aft corners of Carnival Sunshine"; cruisecritic.com Editor's Review confirms wraparound balconies measure ~75 sq ft vs 35 sq ft standard

leads.claim: Sit below the gym area on Deck 10 and may pick up workout-related noise

leads.cabins: Unspecified staterooms near the former dance-club location (pre-2013 Carnival Destiny era)
leads.claim: Historically marketed by Carnival as 'Night Owl Cabins' because they absorbed noise from the dance club above; reportedly fixed in a later dry dock, so current applicability to today's Carnival Sunshine layout is uncertain

unknowns: Whether Carnival Sunshine has any true hull 'hump' (balconies cantilevered past the hull line) — no source found describing this; the wraparound aft-corner balconies are a corner-wrap design, not a confirmed hull bulge.
Whether any high-deck (9–10) suites sit atop a hull taper that hides the straight-down view while keeping the horizon clear — no ship-specific source found for this class.
Precise deck-by-deck location of every elevator/stair bank shaft (only general 'Decks 6–9' guidance found, not a full bank-by-bank map).
Whether the pre-2013 'Night Owl Cabin' noise issue from the old dance club location persists in the post-refit Sunshine layout.
Specific cabin numbers for Deck 5 aft cabins nearest Ocean Plaza/RedFrog Pub/Limelight Lounge (only the general deck/section was confirmed, not exact room ranges).
